newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends up, boosted by Yamasaki comments.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends up, boosted by Yamasaki comments.

text.p: May 12 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 98.88 98.86
Key December three-month euroyen futures ended slightly higher on Monday after getting a boost from comments about interest rates made by a senior member of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).

Taku Yamasaki, chairman of the LDP's policy research council, said on Monday it will not be possible to change the current record-low level of interest rates without further observing the trend of the economy.
Yamasaki said it would become possible to raise interest rates, however, if the economy's recovery becomes full-fledged.

Despite sharp falls last week in euroyen futures due to concerns about a possible rise in interest rates, most market players feel that the Bank of Japan will not be able to raise the official discount rate soon, traders said.
"Market players still take the view that the BOJ needs to see economic data for the April-June period before raising rates," a brokerage house trader said.
The December's turnover during the day session was 95,328 contracts. It moved between 99.85 to 99.90 during the day.

Traders said the December is unlikely to fall further unless fears of a possible rise in interest rates become more prevalent, as the December is already at a level which has factored in a rise in the official discount rate (ODR) within the year.

"I think the December will start moving in a higher range in the near future, especially if the market becomes increasingly convinced that a near-term ODR rise is unlikely," said a trader for a long-term credit bank.
The Bank of Japan drained a net 400 billion yen from the money market on Monday morning.
The BOJ's operation almost totally offest a projected fund surplus of 410 billion yen which the market had going into the day.
It was the first time the central bank had conducted a neutral operation since March 24.
Traders said the BOJ's decision to conduct a neutral operation was based on technical factors.
The BOJ probably decided, after viewing market conditions on Friday, that the overnight call rate was unlikely to rise above 0.50 even with a neutral operation, a trust bank trader said.
Key unsecured overnight call money was most actively traded at 0.47 percent, up slightly from Friday's weighted average of 0.46 percent, a city bank trader said.
No new key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) had been issued as of 0708 GMT. They were offered at 0.57 percent.
About 30 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.54 percent, and about 10 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.55 percent.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, the two- to three-year zones rose as city banks were eager to pay fixed interest rates, a foreign brokerage house trader said.
The three-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.62/66 percent as of 0712 GMT, up from Friday's 1.61/65 percent.
The 10-year IRS rate was quoted at 3.04/08 percent, up from Friday's 3.02/3.06 percent.
The 10-year IRS rate was up in line with a fall in Japanese government bonds, the trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
-- Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-5473-3748
